## India: Regulatory Landscape

The Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Rules, 2025 have been finalized and are expected to be published imminently, marking a crucial step towards the full implementation of India's landmark data protection law. This development follows extensive consultations and will provide essential clarity on the operational aspects of the DPDP Act. ([Source](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisAFBVV95cUxQakx6Y1RYS0lCdGEzN1VfZENmenhLRVZRWUViVUNwZHRCZzhZbDJFYkN4UUdOb1NKZzFKUHdIQnRxWDVINnhTaWY5Ml9IUFppTW44ZkVZeTFzTndwaUo2bl9GYmpHU3U4dkV5UEtGbHdXbG93OGs4QXBSQ3I5Ums5SDFGREdYRHdJQXp2YkpzcTVHaC0wLV9qaDlRRnp2Y25obXhIQVdjSHhsbjZFa0wwTA?oc=5))

MeitY Secretary S. Krishnan confirmed that there would be no extension to the DPDP Act's compliance deadline, urging startups and other entities to ensure their readiness. This firm stance underscores the government's commitment to timely enforcement and signals that businesses must accelerate their data protection preparations. ([Source](https://news.google.?oc=5))

The Supreme Court has requested a response from the Centre regarding Public Interest Litigations (PILs) challenging the constitutionality of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act. This legal scrutiny highlights ongoing debates about various provisions of the Act and could influence its future interpretation. ([Source](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMizwFBVV95cUxOeHEyc3VKdjVZeDNxTzlhNEdIS1B2a19BeHdkRmZYdFQ2d2JjcnlmWFF2aGdoRmxTaHpHNmFMMzV3bVhJc0FFUE1jTVRMVVBmWEhYN0ZUSnJlOUpEWVlpY1NWN1NxalZIVWlEWUlXdnJxUFp5WXBXQUVWYVJENlp0Sm8zd0VqQWVNS2EyRmZnd0p5ZkhqU1lTU3dLcGhpMGs4MVBHRk8za0pHQXN3enZiNnpzQU1weW1zd2xDOUhZUjI4YzlMNUFvaFZqbXhMd2_SAdMBQVVfeXFMUHFqa2haU2I1WkdHc1d2U1B4M3NNVGowQl9HT1huS1M5X1lzSWZydE4wZ190MWxKVjdoZEo1WjJGUVBlYVpoRGZocnFXR1BJWThPVVc0VDA0TktuTVpUVHhRVU04b3pmN1lvTmdMNGYyOGh1dzAwdmhCQllSemNEbmk0QkR0d3hNUTNDU0dvRlgyNUItQnl3ZHFsWHptQ1hMbFV5ZlZvOEY2SU9iUzhxSWtob3RsTzFpb1ZQQVNfY3haeHVpSEJ4VGxBMVQtSzc1WGVIVQ?oc=5))

MeitY informed Parliament that Common Service Centre (CSC) operators are prohibited from storing Aadhaar or banking data. This directive aims to enhance data security and prevent misuse of sensitive personal information handled by CSCs, reinforcing specific data handling obligations under the broader privacy framework. ([Source](https://news.google.?oc=5))

## India: DPDPA in Practice

The DPDP Act significantly impacts workplace surveillance practices, requiring employers to carefully balance legitimate business interests with employee privacy rights. Organizations must re-evaluate their monitoring policies and ensure they meet the new standards for consent and data processing. ([Source](https://news.google.?oc=5))

## Global & Cross-Border Insights

Reconciling India's DPDP Act with the EU's GDPR presents a complex challenge for cross-border transfers of healthcare data, particularly for Indian businesses operating globally. The differing legal bases for processing and transfer mechanisms necessitate careful consideration to ensure compliance across jurisdictions.
